findings.description: [qodo] The startup banner resolves FORGE_LLM_TIMEOUT_S from os.environ rather than the `env` mapping passed to _run, and the displayed timeout is computed with effective_invoke_timeout_s(backend, None) rather than that same env value. With no backend timeout and FORGE_LLM_TIMEOUT_S set, this can print a timeout value/source that is internally inconsistent or wrong: the banner may claim '(from FORGE_LLM_TIMEOUT_S)' while the displayed seconds were resolved as if the env var were absent. Use the same environment/value for both the timeout lookup and the banner note.

[qodo] _banner_timeout_note treats any non-None env_raw as if the env override is honored. An empty FORGE_LLM_TIMEOUT_S= will still append '(from FORGE_LLM_TIMEOUT_S)' even though the resolver likely ignores an empty or invalid value. Guard on truthiness/validated integer so the banner does not claim an env override that is not in effect.

[expert] Broad `except SystemExit` at the main pipeline boundary treats every `SystemExit` as an internal error. If argparse `--help`/`--version` or an early-exit path in a nested subcommand runs inside this try, normal `sys.exit(0)`/`sys.exit(2)` behavior becomes a traceback and EXIT_CLI_ERROR. Keep argument-parser exits outside this catch, or narrow it to the exact call that must not call `sys.exit`.

[expert] `_repo_display_name` returns `repo_name` from the git top-level path or `cwd.name` without sanitizing control or ANSI characters, and `_startup_banner_line` writes it directly to stderr. A repository directory name containing newlines or escape sequences can corrupt the terminal/log line. The timeout env var is sanitized for exactly this reason; apply the same printable-character filter or truncation to the repo name.

[adversarial] The new `except SystemExit` is a sibling to the broad `except Exception` in `main()`'s top-level try block that also wraps argument parsing. argparse raises `SystemExit` for normal `--help`, `--version`, and usage errors; those are now captured here, printed as internal errors with tracebacks, and returned as EXIT_CLI_ERROR. This converts `code-forge --help`/`--version` from successful exits into internal-error exits. Let argparse's SystemExit propagate, or move parse_args outside this try so only pipeline-originated SystemExit is converted.

[adversarial] `_banner_timeout` is computed by calling `effective_invoke_timeout_s(backend, None)`, while the banner suffix is computed from `os.environ.get("FORGE_LLM_TIMEOUT_S")` in `_banner_timeout_note`. The resolution chain does not use `None` when the env override is present, so with `FORGE_LLM_TIMEOUT_S` set and no backend timeout, the banner can print a timeout that ignores the env var while appending `(from FORGE_LLM_TIMEOUT_S)`. Pass the same env value used by the actual timeout resolution to both the effective-timeout call and the note computation.

[adversarial] `_banner_timeout_note` only checks `env_raw is None`. An empty `FORGE_LLM_TIMEOUT_S=''` is therefore treated as an honored override and produces `(from FORGE_LLM_TIMEOUT_S)`, even though empty timeout env vars are normally treated as unset by the resolution chain. Treat empty/whitespace-only values as unset to avoid a misleading banner suffix.
